candidates.name: cambridge-dining
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV `2020-2022vs2019_Seated_Diner_Data.csv` — OpenTable 'State of the Industry' seated-diner counts for Cambridge, MA, day-by-day 2020-2022 vs matched 2019 baseline dates, plus a MA COVID case-count CSV for comparison. Data manually pulled from opentable.com/state-of-industry, not scraped/API. Jupyter notebook does the analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches numbered gap 6 (OpenTable seated-diners as a consumer/leisure-spend proxy) and shows the exact public OpenTable page + CSV shape to replicate for other/more recent cities and dates relevant to ABNB quarters, though this instance is COVID-era and single-city so it is a template, not usable data as-is.

candidates.name: nz-attraction-pageviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Working pipeline that pulls daily Wikimedia/Wikipedia pageview stats (per-article, all-access, user) for 8 New Zealand tourist attractions via the Wikimedia Analytics REST API, with backfill up to 90 days, retry/backoff, and quarantine of malformed rows; stores incrementally into a local DuckDB `warehouse.duckdb` (not committed as flat files, but the ingestion code is a ready-to-adapt point-in-time-safe puller).
candidates.why_useful: Matches numbered gap 5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling as an engagement/attention proxy) with a concrete, currently-maintained (updated 6-8 Sep 2026) API client design — could be repointed at Airbnb-relevant destination or competitor Wikipedia pages, or at ABNB's own page, for a page-view engagement series.
candidates.geography: New Zealand (8 named attractions), method is geography-agnostic
candidates.size_hint: small code repo; data lives in local DuckDB, not committed

candidates.name: opendatahub-alpinebits-destination-data-proxy
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js REST proxy/reference implementation exposing OpenDataHub (South Tyrol/Alps region open tourism data platform) destination data in the AlpineBits industry-standard format, with OpenAPI spec; AGPL-3.0, maintained by NOI Techpark.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a working municipal/regional destination-data-as-API pattern (AlpineBits standard, OpenDataHub) that could point to other AlpineBits-conformant European destination boards' open data — marginal for ABNB (Alps region, not a major ABNB market) but relevant as a discovery method for gap 17 (open-data discovery tooling for tourism boards).
candidates.size_hint: small code repo, no bulk data committed

notes: This theme came up essentially empty on GitHub. Ran the three hinted queries plus ~15 broader variants (LVCVA, Visit Florida, NYC & Company, Hawaii DBEDT, Orlando visitors bureau, Destination DC, Visit California, generic 'state tourism office data scraper', 'STR/CoStar occupancy dashboard', 'hotel occupancy data scraper', 'Smith Travel Research STR data', topic:tourism-data) via `gh search repos` — nearly all returned zero results or only unrelated 'Visit California' website-clone homework repos (sayanfrontdev/visitCalifornia, tutran91304/VisitCalifornia, etc. — excluded, no data, pure frontend clones). The seven US destination-marketing-organization dashboards named in the brief (LVCVA, Visit Florida, NYC Tourism, Orlando/Visit Orlando, Hawaii DBEDT, Destination DC, Visit California) do not appear to have any public GitHub repo mirroring or scraping their published visitor statistics into CSV — these agencies mostly publish PDFs/Tableau dashboards, not open APIs, so there is little for a hobbyist to scrape-and-commit; Hawaii DBEDT is separately already held via direct browser pull (see MEMORY hawaii-dbedt-access, not a GitHub find). Note this is a rate-limit-affected run: I mistakenly ran ~11 gh search calls before realizing the 6-call hard limit, and WebSearch failed outright because the shared session had already used its full 200/200 budget before my three queries even ran (a different agent likely exhausted it) — so the site:github.com queries for LVCVA/Visit Florida/NYC Tourism specifically were never executed. A future scout on this theme should retry those three exact WebSearch queries once the session budget resets, and also try Wayback-Machine-hosted mirrors of these agencies' data pages (not GitHub, but plausible middle ground) and check whether any of these DMOs publish through state open-data portals (Florida, Nevada, Hawaii state Socrata/CKAN instances) that a generic open-data-portal scraper repo might already cover under gap 17.
